problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}a+2b=5 \\ -3a+8b=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$a=$
{{field-1}}$,\,b=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}a+2b=5 & |\,\times 4 \\ -3a+8b=-4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3a+8b=20 \\ -3a+8b=-4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $3a$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-3a$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $a$-variable, and allows us to solve for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{3a}+8b & =20 \\ -\cancel{3a}+8b & =-4 \\ 16b & =16 \\ b & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $b=1$ into the equation $-3a+8b=-4$ to solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3a+8b & =-4 \\ -3a+8\cdot 1 & =-4 \\ -3a+8 & =-4 \\ -3a & =-12 \\ a & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=4$ and $b=1.$
